extra.message: WebSocket message data (chatMessage.author.name and chatMessage.message) is attacker-controlled and is concatenated directly into p.innerHTML without sanitization. A malicious chat message such as is parsed as HTML and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser (DOM-based stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: user.emailAddress is user-controlled (supplied via the public registration form) and is passed directly to jQuery's replaceWith(), which parses the string as HTML. A stored payload in the email address field executes when another user clicks 'Click to show contact' (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: user.webPageUrl (attacker-controlled at registration) is rendered into an anchor with target="_blank" and no rel="noopener noreferrer". The opened page can access window.opener and navigate the victim's tab (reverse tabnabbing). Because this app uses React 15.6.1, javascript: URLs are not blocked, so a javascript: webPageUrl can also execute script in the app origin.

cwe: CWE-1022: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access

extra.message: The STOMP/SockJS WebSocket connection authenticates with hardcoded credentials ('asdf'/'were') instead of the logged-in user's session. Every client uses the same shared identity, so the server cannot distinguish or authorize individual users for the /user/queue/notifications queue, allowing one user to receive another user's notifications.

State-changing PUT to messages/chat is sent with credentials:'include' (cookie-based session) but no anti-CSRF token or Origin/Referer validation. A malicious third-party page can force a logged-in victim's browser to send chat messages on their behalf.

State-changing PUT to the user creation endpoint is sent with credentials:'include' and no anti-CSRF token. An attacker-controlled page can cause a logged-in victim's browser to issue this request (e.g. create/modify accounts) without the victim's intent.
Logout is performed via an unauthenticated GET request with credentials:'include' and no CSRF token. A third-party page can embed this URL (e.g. ) to force the victim to be logged out (CSRF).

The backend base URLs are hardcoded as plaintext http:// (http://35.204.241.43:31337/). Login credentials (username/password) and session cookies are transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, allowing network attackers to intercept them.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
